preamble: The voiceless retroflex fricative [ʂ] loses its retroflexion and becomes the postalveolar [ʃ]. The clearest cases are Indo-Aryan: Sanskrit ṣ [ʂ] is commonly pronounced [ʃ] in Hindi and Urdu, and it merged with ś as /ʃ/ in Bengali. Southern and Taiwan Mandarin deretroflexion goes to [s], not [ʃ] (see sh_retroflex_to_s).

examples.note: Retroflex /ʂ/ of Sanskrit loanwords is usually replaced by /ʃ/ in casual Hindi and in Urdu.
Learned borrowing; Bengali ষ is pronounced [ʃ], like শ.

sources: Masica, C. P. (1991). The Indo-Aryan Languages. Cambridge University Press. https://www.cambridge.org/9780521299442
